items.question:
A data engineer at a 500-person e-commerce company is advising the merchandising team on how to surface inventory availability in a Claude Project. Stock levels change hourly as orders are placed and fulfilment happens. The team is deciding between a daily batch export (uploaded each morning) and a real-time connector.

Which factor is MOST decisive in choosing between them?

options.A: Whether the inventory system's API supports the connector format required by the platform.
options.B: How significantly a product's availability status changing within the day would affect a merchandiser's decisions.
options.C: Whether the data team has bandwidth to set up and maintain a connector integration.
options.D: The volume of inventory records, since larger datasets are better suited to batch exports.

items.question:
A product manager at a software company finds two files in a Claude Project: 'PRD_v2.docx' and 'Product_Requirements_Final.docx'. Their content overlaps significantly but is not identical. A developer complains that Claude's requirement summaries differ between sessions.

What does this situation MOST likely represent?

options.A: Two valid requirement documents representing different product areas that should be merged.
options.B: Two documents in deliberate parallel development that should remain separate.
options.C: Unintended duplicate copies of the same requirements document at different revision stages, creating version confusion.
options.D: A version conflict caused by two product teams using different naming conventions for the same artefact.

items.question:
An account manager at a professional services firm is considering adding a specific client's pricing proposal and master services agreement to a Claude Project shared with 12 other account managers who each serve different clients.

What is the PRIMARY concern with this approach?

options.A: The pricing proposal format may not be parsed accurately by Claude.
options.B: Other account managers may not have the seniority to access another client's commercial terms.
options.C: The document file size may degrade Project performance for other users.
options.D: Client-specific confidential documents in a shared Project create a confidentiality risk: other account managers' conversations could inadvertently draw on a different client's terms.

items.question:
An underwriter at an insurance broker has two versions of the company's risk appetite guide: a narrative document with thresholds described in paragraphs, and a structured table with risk categories, threshold values, and policy limits in named columns. Both contain identical information.

Which format BETTER supports Claude extracting specific threshold values when answering underwriting questions?

options.A: The structured table, because named columns and explicit threshold values give Claude direct extraction targets.
options.B: The narrative document, because prose provides richer context around each threshold's rationale.
options.C: Both formats equally, since the information content is identical.
options.D: The narrative document, because Claude processes natural language more accurately than structured data.

items.question:
A research scientist at a pharmaceutical company considers splitting a 40-page clinical trial protocol into section-level files: eligibility criteria, dosing schedule, adverse event reporting, and endpoint definitions. The protocol requires cross-referencing across sections — for example, eligibility criteria reference dosing thresholds, and endpoint definitions reference adverse event criteria.

What is the PRIMARY risk of splitting this document?

options.A: Splitting reduces the total word count available to Claude, which may cause it to miss important details.
options.B: Splitting removes the cross-referencing context that allows Claude to reconcile inter-section dependencies when answering protocol questions.
options.C: Splitting is only appropriate for documents over 100 pages; a 40-page document is too short to benefit.
options.D: Claude cannot process multiple files from the same source document in a single conversation.

items.question:
A finance manager at a retail chain has four budget templates in a Claude Project: monthly, quarterly, annual, and reforecast. All four are currently named generically (BudgetTemplate.xlsx, BudgetTemplate2.xlsx, BudgetTemplate3.xlsx, BudgetTemplate4.xlsx). Users frequently report loading the wrong template.

What naming convention would MOST directly reduce confusion?

options.A: Use sequential letters (BudgetTemplate_A through BudgetTemplate_D) and maintain a separate legend.
options.B: Keep the generic names and add a Project instruction explaining which number corresponds to which cycle.
options.C: Name each template to include the cycle type and its primary use case (e.g., BudgetTemplate_Monthly_Variance.xlsx).
options.D: Name them by the user role that primarily uses them (e.g., BudgetTemplate_RegionalManager.xlsx).

items.question:
A customer success manager at a SaaS company wants to add customer health scores from the CSM platform to a Claude Project. Health scores recalculate weekly. He is deciding between a weekly manual export and a real-time connector. The setup cost of the connector is moderate.

What factor is MOST decisive in this decision?

options.A: Whether the CS team has technical expertise to configure and maintain the connector.
options.B: The number of customers whose health scores would be surfaced in the Project.
options.C: Whether the CSM platform vendor provides official connector support.
options.D: How materially week-old health score data would affect the quality of the CS team's at-risk customer decisions.

items.question:
A solutions architect at a fintech startup is building a workflow where Claude answers questions about individual customer accounts. Each customer service agent has a different assigned customer. She is debating whether to use a Claude Project connector to surface account data, or to inject each customer's account summary directly into the per-conversation prompt.

In which scenario does per-prompt context injection BEAT a permanent connector?

options.A: When the account data is customer-specific and should not be accessible across different agents' sessions in a shared Project.
options.B: When the account data volume exceeds what the connector can synchronise in real time.
options.C: When the connector setup process requires IT approval, creating a deployment delay.
options.D: When the account data schema changes frequently, causing connector mapping errors.

items.question:
An IT operations manager at a 900-person healthcare system has placed the company's IT security policy in both the Project knowledge base and in the Project's custom instructions (system prompt). A junior analyst notices that Claude's security guidance differs between sessions — sometimes citing one standard, sometimes citing a slightly different formulation.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The custom instructions in the Project always override Project knowledge, so the policy in knowledge is being ignored.
options.B: Having the same content in both Project knowledge and the system prompt creates reference ambiguity that Claude resolves inconsistently across sessions.
options.C: Claude only uses one source for any given query, so the inconsistency must be caused by a different file.
options.D: The inconsistency is caused by the format difference between a policy document and a prompt instruction.

items.question:
A policy analyst at a government ministry must decide whether to split a 150-page integrated policy document into separate files by policy area, or to keep it as one document with clear headings. Queries from staff frequently span multiple policy areas — for example, asking how a housing regulation interacts with a planning policy.

What principle BEST governs this decision?

options.A: Split documents are always preferable to single large documents because they improve retrieval speed.
options.B: The document should always remain whole to preserve legal integrity and prevent misquotation of clauses in isolation.
options.C: If queries regularly require synthesising across policy areas, keeping the document whole preserves cross-area context; if queries are consistently area-specific, splitting improves retrieval.
options.D: The decision should be based on the document's total page count, with documents over 100 pages always split.

items.question:
A compliance operations manager at a wealth management firm has completed an audit of a shared Claude Project and documented three issues: (1) three regulatory guidance notes from two years ago remain in Project knowledge; (2) the current KYC policy exists under two different filenames; (3) several client-specific due diligence files were added by an analyst and should not be in a shared Project. She has finished documenting all three issues.

What should she do NEXT?

options.A: Email the Project owner all three findings and wait for written approval before making any changes.
options.B: Remove only the client-specific files as the most urgent risk, then schedule the outdated guidance and duplicate KYC for a later review cycle.
options.C: Add Project custom instructions flagging which documents should not be consulted, then schedule deletions for the next maintenance window.
options.D: Remove all three categories of problematic content in one remediation session, then run verification queries across the affected areas to confirm the knowledge base is clean.

items.question: An operations analyst at a 3,000-person manufacturing company is recommending data sources for a Claude Project. Which TWO scenarios MOST justify using a connector rather than a periodic static upload? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Machine downtime alerts that update every 15 minutes as production line status changes.
options.B: Daily production yield summaries that the quality team reviews each morning for variance analysis.
options.C: The plant's emergency evacuation procedures, reviewed and updated annually.
options.D: A six-month-old industry benchmarking report on equipment efficiency, published annually.
options.E: The supplier onboarding checklist, revised when relevant regulations change.

items.question: A knowledge manager at a 200-person management consulting firm is deciding which documents in a Claude Project knowledge base should be split into smaller files. Which TWO situations MOST justify splitting a document? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The document was uploaded more than six months ago.
options.B: The document is formatted as a PDF rather than a Word file.
options.C: The document covers five distinct service offerings and queries consistently ask about one offering at a time.
options.D: The document is 120 pages long and Claude's answers to section-specific questions are consistently too general.
options.E: The document is the only file currently in the Project knowledge base.

items.question: A content operations manager at a 600-person media company is establishing versioning standards for a Claude Project shared across 15 editors. Which TWO practices MOST directly prevent version-related errors in Project knowledge? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Store all previous document versions in a subfolder within Project knowledge so editors can reference revision history.
options.B: When uploading a new version, remove the prior version in the same session before finalising the upload.
options.C: Name all files with a sequential version counter suffix (v1, v2, v3) to maintain traceability within the Project.
options.D: Add a Project instruction telling Claude to prefer the document with the highest version number when multiple versions exist.
options.E: Maintain a document register outside the Project that records the current version of each file and its last review date.

items.question: A data architect at a global financial services firm is advising the knowledge management team on document structure standards for Claude Project knowledge. Which THREE properties MOST improve a document's retrievability within a Claude Project? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Clear, specific section headings that name the entity, process, or policy each section covers.
options.B: A comprehensive table of contents at the start listing every section.
options.C: Compressing all documents into a single ZIP archive to reduce storage overhead.
options.D: Filenames that include the document type, subject area, and date of last review.
options.E: Content organised with consistent bullet points and tables rather than dense unstructured paragraphs.

items.question:
An HR manager at a 500-person retail company adds the full employee directory — including names, titles, emails, and salaries — to a Claude Project shared with all 18 department heads. She reasons that the data is already accessible internally and that heads need it for workforce planning.

What is the MOST significant risk introduced?

options.A: Salary data and contact details in a shared AI Project expand the exposure surface beyond the directory's original access controls, creating a sensitive data governance risk.
options.B: The file size of the directory may degrade Project performance for other users.
options.C: Department heads may ask Claude to produce reports that violate the organisation's reporting line structure.
options.D: The directory will become stale as employees join and leave, producing incorrect workforce planning outputs.

items.question:
A legal operations manager at a law firm reviews a Claude Project set up 18 months ago for contract drafting. None of the documents have been reviewed or updated since the initial launch. The firm has updated several standard clause positions and adopted a new indemnity framework in that period.

Which risk MOST warrants immediate attention?

options.A: The Project may have accumulated unused conversations that are reducing performance.
options.B: Documents that reference clause positions or policy frameworks may have been superseded by changes made in the past 18 months.
options.C: The Project's custom instructions may no longer reflect the current lead partner's preferences.
options.D: The original Project creator may have left the firm, leaving no one responsible for the Project.

items.question:
A research analyst at a pharmaceutical company adds a proprietary database export in a binary encoding format to a Claude Project knowledge base. When she later asks Claude questions that should draw on this data source, Claude's responses are vague and do not reference any of the expected figures.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.A: The database export is too large for Claude to fully process during a single conversation.
options.B: The export contains numerical data, which Claude handles less accurately than text content.
options.C: The file's binary format is not readable as text content, so the data is unavailable to Claude despite the file being present in the knowledge base.
options.D: The file must be uploaded per-conversation rather than stored in Project knowledge to be accessible.

items.question:
An operations lead at an 80-person logistics startup has added 60 documents to a Claude Project over 18 months — meeting notes, email threads, vendor contracts, archived process documents, and reference guides — treating it as a general file repository. Users report that Claude's operational guidance has become increasingly generic and unhelpful.

What is the PRIMARY cause of the declining quality?

options.A: The Project's context window is being exceeded by the volume of documents.
options.B: Sixty documents is beyond the recommended maximum for any Claude Project.
options.C: The vendor contracts introduce legal language that confuses Claude's operational guidance.
options.D: The large volume of irrelevant operational and archived content is diluting the signal from reference documents, producing generic responses.

items.question:
A strategy analyst at a consulting firm inadvertently adds an internal pricing model to a client-facing Claude Project shared with three clients. During a client conversation, Claude surfaces internal margin figures that the client should not have seen. The analyst has just been informed.

What should the analyst do FIRST?

options.A: Remove the pricing model from Project knowledge immediately to prevent any further exposure.
options.B: Ask Claude to confirm whether it referenced the pricing model in any client conversations.
options.C: Notify all three clients that an error occurred and that the shared Project has been suspended.
options.D: Move the pricing model to a password-protected subfolder within the Project.

items.question:
A 50-person software company has its product team and marketing team sharing a single Claude Project. The product team's technical specifications and API documentation share a knowledge base with the marketing team's brand guidelines, customer messaging frameworks, and campaign briefs. Both teams report that Claude's responses feel off-tone and mismatched for their work.

What is the root cause?

options.A: The Project's custom instructions do not distinguish between the two teams' preferred output formats.
options.B: A single knowledge base serving two workflows with different vocabularies and reference documents produces responses that are incoherent for both.
options.C: The technical documentation is in a different file format from the marketing documents, causing retrieval conflicts.
options.D: The combined document volume exceeds what a single Project can serve reliably.

items.question:
A sales operations manager at a SaaS company configured a CRM connector for a Claude Project six weeks ago. Account executives initially praised the current deal data. In the last two weeks, AEs have reported that deal stages and contact details are becoming stale again.

What is the MOST appropriate first diagnostic step?

options.A: Re-upload a static CRM export as a temporary fix while the connector is investigated.
options.B: Assume the connector is working and that the CRM data itself has not been updated by the AEs.
options.C: Investigate the connector's synchronisation status, credentials, and last successful sync timestamp.
options.D: Replace the connector with a static weekly export since connectors are unreliable long-term.

items.question:
Three months after launching a Claude Project for the underwriting team at a 400-person insurance company, a knowledge manager discovers that two of the six Project knowledge documents reference a product tier that was discontinued two months ago. The underwriting team has been receiving incorrect guidance for eight weeks.

What process would MOST effectively prevent this failure from recurring?

options.A: Schedule a comprehensive quarterly review of all Project knowledge documents.
options.B: Increase the frequency of knowledge base reviews to weekly.
options.C: Limit the knowledge base to three documents so reviews can be completed faster.
options.D: Establish a trigger-based review process so that when any product is changed or discontinued, all affected knowledge documents are immediately audited.

items.question:
Over 12 months, a content manager at a B2B technology company has been adding documents to a Claude Project originally created for blog and website content creation. The Project now contains the original editorial guidelines alongside technical product documentation, investor relations materials, and internal strategy documents. Blog draft quality has declined noticeably.

What BEST explains the decline?

options.A: The off-scope documents introduce irrelevant content that dilutes Claude's focus on the editorial reference material when generating blog drafts.
options.B: The increased document count slows Claude's processing time, reducing response quality.
options.C: The investor relations and strategy documents contain confidential language that Claude filters out of its responses.
options.D: The technical documentation contains specialised terminology that conflicts with the editorial guidelines.

items.question:
An M&A analyst at an investment bank adds a competitor company's board presentation to a shared Claude Project. The presentation was obtained through a third-party intelligence data service. Six weeks later, the legal team flags that the data service's terms of use prohibit use of obtained materials in AI analysis or processing tools.

What was the PRIMARY governance failure?

options.A: The analyst added a competitor document to a shared Project rather than a private one.
options.B: The analyst did not verify that the third-party data service licence permits use of its materials in an AI processing tool before uploading.
options.C: The board presentation should have been summarised by the analyst before uploading to avoid direct reproduction of third-party content.
options.D: Competitive intelligence documents should never be added to Claude Projects under any circumstances.

items.question:
A tax manager at a mid-market manufacturer has a Claude Project for VAT return preparation. A Project knowledge document containing VAT guidance was last updated 22 months ago. A legislative change 10 months ago altered a key VAT threshold. The company's last three quarterly submissions used the pre-change threshold based on Claude's guidance.

What process change would have MOST directly prevented this?

options.A: Using Claude for a different VAT preparation tool rather than relying on Project knowledge.
options.B: Uploading VAT guidance only per-conversation rather than storing it in Project knowledge.
options.C: Establishing a process to review affected Project knowledge documents each time a relevant tax legislation change is announced.
options.D: Running all VAT submissions through a separate tax software system before using Claude's output.

items.question:
A compliance manager at a global bank has a Claude Project containing 12 versions of the credit risk policy — one per geographic region — with minor but material differences in exposure limits. When analysts ask Claude about exposure thresholds for a specific region, Claude frequently synthesises rules from multiple regional versions rather than citing the relevant region's policy.

What is the BEST structural fix?

options.A: Add a Project instruction telling Claude to ask the user for their region before answering exposure questions.
options.B: Merge all 12 regional policies into a single master document with a regional comparison table.
options.C: Create a separate Claude Project for each region so there is no cross-regional contamination.
options.D: Ensure each regional policy file is named to include the region, and add clear internal headings identifying the geographic scope.

items.question:
An IT administrator at a hospital removes a former employee from a shared Claude Project following their departure. The former employee had been the primary curator of the Project over 18 months and had added 14 of the 20 documents in the knowledge base.

What additional action is REQUIRED?

options.A: Review all 14 documents added by the former employee to verify they are still current, in scope, and do not contain inappropriate content.
options.B: Delete all 14 documents added by the former employee and ask the new curator to rebuild the knowledge base from scratch.
options.C: Keep the existing documents unchanged since removing the employee from the Project has already resolved the access risk.
options.D: Add a Project instruction noting that some documents were added by a former employee and their currency cannot be guaranteed.

items.question:
A legal counsel at an energy company discovers that a Project knowledge document contains a materially incorrect contract clause position that has been producing wrong guidance. The document is subject to a formal records retention policy in the firm's document management system that prevents immediate deletion from official records.

What is the BEST approach while awaiting formal deletion approval?

options.A: Add a custom instruction warning Claude never to reference the specific document.
options.B: Remove the incorrect document from Project knowledge and replace it with a corrected version, while retaining the original in the firm's document management system as required by the retention policy.
options.C: Leave the Project unchanged and notify users manually of the known error until deletion is approved.
options.D: Delete the document immediately from both the Project and the records management system to prevent further harm.

items.question:
A data protection officer at a pharmaceutical company reviews a request to add clinical trial summary reports to a Claude Project used by the regulatory affairs team. The reports contain aggregate patient-level statistics derived from trial data. The company's data governance policy requires a formal AI risk assessment before any patient-derived data is processed in an external AI tool.

What should the DPO do?

options.A: Approve the addition since the reports contain aggregate statistics, not individual patient records, so the risk assessment requirement does not apply.
options.B: Require the data to be further aggregated or anonymised before the risk assessment is initiated.
options.C: Require the formal risk assessment to be completed before any patient-derived data — regardless of aggregation level — is added to the Project.
options.D: Allow the regulatory affairs team to proceed if they confirm the data will only be used for internal regulatory submissions.

items.question:
An operations manager at an 80-person professional services firm takes over a Claude Project that has not been maintained for 14 months. He has catalogued three issues: (a) three documents reference a service offering discontinued 12 months ago; (b) the main operations manual was uploaded without headings and produces generic responses; (c) a connector previously linked to a CRM that was decommissioned eight months ago is still configured. He has finished the audit.

What should he do NEXT?

options.A: Address only the discontinued-service documents first, as they pose the most immediate accuracy risk, and defer the structural and connector issues for a subsequent sprint.
options.B: Disable the broken connector first, since a connector pointing to a decommissioned system may generate error states, then plan the other remediations.
options.C: Add custom instructions flagging all three known issues so current users are informed while a full remediation plan is developed.
options.D: Execute all three remediations in a single session — remove the discontinued-service documents, restructure the operations manual, decommission the connector — then verify with test queries.

items.question: A knowledge governance lead at a financial services firm is reviewing several Claude Projects. Which TWO conditions indicate that a Project knowledge base requires IMMEDIATE corrective action? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Claude cited a product that was discontinued nine months ago as currently available to a customer-facing analyst.
options.B: The Project currently contains six documents, which the team considers a modest number.
options.C: A user reported that Claude gave two substantively contradictory answers to the same compliance question in different sessions.
options.D: The Project was created by an employee who left the company three months ago.
options.E: The most recently added document is 80 pages long and covers multiple product lines.

items.question: A procurement manager at a public sector organisation wants to add completed supplier due diligence reports to a Claude Project shared with eight procurement analysts. Which TWO governance steps are MOST important to complete BEFORE uploading? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Convert the reports to plain text format to ensure consistent parsing by Claude.
options.B: Verify that the organisation's data classification policy permits storing supplier due diligence data in an AI platform.
options.C: Remove all quantitative metrics from the reports before uploading to reduce sensitivity.
options.D: Confirm that uploading the reports does not breach confidentiality obligations or NDAs with the suppliers.
options.E: Ensure each report file is below the organisation's individual file upload limit before proceeding.

items.question: A knowledge manager at a 200-person professional services firm oversees a Claude Project shared with 30 consultants. Which THREE practices MOST effectively maintain knowledge base quality over an 18-month operational period? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Designate a named owner for each document who is accountable for keeping it current and removing it when it is no longer needed.
options.B: Establish a process for removing a document when the business process it supports is discontinued or significantly changed.
options.C: Cap the total number of documents at a fixed maximum to prevent the knowledge base from growing beyond an agreed threshold.
options.D: Create a mirror of the Project knowledge in a backup Project in case the primary becomes unavailable.
options.E: Conduct a periodic review of all documents against a defined scope statement to identify and remove off-topic additions.

items.question: A financial analyst at an investment fund must decide between per-chat upload and Project knowledge for several document types. Which TWO should use per-chat upload rather than Project knowledge? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The fund's investment mandate and risk appetite policy, reviewed and approved annually.
options.B: A standard due diligence checklist used in every deal review across the team.
options.C: A specific portfolio company's recent earnings call transcript, relevant only for today's investment committee discussion.
options.D: A glossary of financial instruments and deal terminology used by all analysts.
options.E: A confidential draft term sheet for a live deal currently under negotiation, not yet executed.

items.question:
A treasury analyst at an energy company uses Claude every business day to analyse interest rate exposures. She uses a rate table that updates each business day. She is deciding whether to add it to a Claude Project's knowledge base or upload it per-chat each morning.

What is the MOST appropriate approach?

options.A: Upload per-chat each morning or configure a connector; do not add a static version to Project knowledge because it will be stale within 24 hours.
options.B: Add the rate table to Project knowledge and set a reminder to re-upload it each business day.
options.C: Add the rate table to Project knowledge once, since the analyst reviews it daily in any case.
options.D: Upload the rate table per-conversation on alternating days to balance freshness with convenience.

items.question: A marketing coordinator at a hotel group uploads an updated campaign brief to a shared Claude Project as 'CampaignBrief_Final_REVISED.docx' without removing the original 'CampaignBrief.docx'. The original and the revision have different messaging priorities. What is the IMMEDIATE action required?

options.A: Add a Project instruction telling Claude to use the document with 'REVISED' in its name.
options.B: Remove the original 'CampaignBrief.docx' from Project knowledge to eliminate the version conflict.
options.C: Merge the original and the revised brief into a single definitive document.
options.D: Rename both documents with upload dates to help Claude identify the newer one.

items.question:
A strategy consultant adds a one-off industry landscape report, produced for a specific client engagement, to a Claude Project shared with five other consultants working on different client matters. The report is specific to that client's sector and competitive context.

What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.A: Keep the report in Project knowledge since industry context is useful background for all client work.
options.B: Archive the report within the Project knowledge base once the engagement closes.
options.C: Remove the client-specific report from Project knowledge and use per-chat upload if references to it are still needed.
options.D: Compress the report into a summary before re-uploading it to reduce its contribution to scope creep.

items.question:
A compensation analyst at a manufacturing firm maintains a Claude Project shared with five HR managers for pay review support. She wants to use current pay band data in the Project. The pay band details should only be visible to three of the five HR managers — the core compensation team.

What is the MOST appropriate approach for the pay band data?

options.A: Add the pay band data to Project knowledge with a note that it is restricted to the compensation team.
options.B: Encrypt the pay band file before adding it to Project knowledge.
options.C: Add the pay band data to Project knowledge since all five are HR managers with appropriate clearance.
options.D: Use per-chat upload for the pay band data rather than adding it to the shared Project.

items.question:
A policy manager at an insurance company has a 60-page general insurance product manual covering motor, home, and life insurance. Users ask Claude product-specific questions about one product at a time, never cross-product questions.

What document structure would MOST improve response accuracy?

options.A: Split the manual into three separate files — one per product — with descriptive filenames reflecting the product type.
options.B: Upload the full 60-page manual with an executive summary at the front.
options.C: Add a Project instruction telling Claude to always specify the product at the start of each response.
options.D: Convert the manual to a table of thresholds and limits for each product type.

items.question:
A compliance manager at a global bank maintains a Claude Project for regulatory analysis, shared with 20 analysts. She updates Project knowledge with official regulatory guidance as it is published. Recently two analysts have been uploading their own interpretation notes alongside the official guidance, causing Claude to blend authoritative source documents with unofficial commentary.

What governance change BEST prevents this?

options.A: Add a Project instruction distinguishing between official guidance and analyst interpretation notes.
options.B: Restrict write access to Project knowledge to the compliance manager only, removing analysts' ability to add documents.
options.C: Create a designated folder within Project knowledge for analyst notes.
options.D: Conduct a monthly audit to remove analyst-added content that has accumulated.

items.question:
An operations manager's Claude Project was created for supply chain planning. Over 18 months it has expanded to include customer service scripts, store opening procedures, and HR onboarding guides. The supply chain team now reports that Claude's logistics and procurement guidance has become too generic.

What is the BEST approach to restore quality while keeping the supply chain Project operational?

options.A: Upgrade to a higher-tier model to improve retrieval across the larger knowledge base.
options.B: Add per-conversation context specifying that Claude should focus only on supply chain content.
options.C: Remove all documents not directly relevant to supply chain planning and create separate Projects for the other workflows.
options.D: Add a custom instruction specifying that Claude should only draw on supply chain documents when answering supply chain questions.

items.question:
A risk manager at an investment bank discovers that a new capital regulation announced last week affects provisions in three of the six documents in a Claude Project used for risk reporting. She has identified exactly which three are affected.

What is the CORRECT action?

options.A: Add a Project instruction noting that capital regulation guidance may have changed recently.
options.B: Remove all six documents and rebuild the knowledge base once the new regulation is fully understood.
options.C: Update only the document that most directly references capital requirements and leave the others pending.
options.D: Update all three affected documents with the revised regulatory provisions and remove the outdated versions in the same session.

items.question:
An account manager uses a Claude Project for client meeting preparation. She needs: (a) live CRM account data that changes daily; (b) a client-specific briefing document she prepared for today's meeting; (c) the firm's standard client engagement methodology that applies to all client work.

What combination of approaches is MOST appropriate?

options.A: CRM data via connector, client briefing per-chat, methodology in Project knowledge.
options.B: All three in Project knowledge for maximum context continuity.
options.C: CRM data and methodology in Project knowledge, client briefing per-chat.
options.D: All three per-chat each session for maximum freshness.

items.question:
A commercial manager at an energy company has eight contract templates in a Claude Project — one per jurisdiction (UK, Germany, France, USA, Australia, Singapore, UAE, India). All are named 'ContractTemplate_V3.docx' through 'ContractTemplate_V10.docx'. Users regularly load the wrong template.

What naming change would MOST directly resolve this?

options.A: Rename them with sequential letters (A through H) to replace the version counter.
options.B: Rename each template to include the jurisdiction (e.g., ContractTemplate_Germany_V3.docx).
options.C: Add a Project instruction mapping each version number to its corresponding jurisdiction.
options.D: Combine all eight into a single document with clearly labelled jurisdiction-specific sections.

items.question:
A legal operations manager at a law firm learns that a senior partner — the sole curator of a critical Claude Project used daily by associates for matter research — is leaving the firm in two weeks. The Project contains 18 knowledge documents accumulated over two years.

What is the CORRECT planning action?

options.A: Archive the Project immediately to prevent unauthorised changes during the transition.
options.B: Wait until after the partner departs to decide whether the Project needs a new curator.
options.C: Designate a new curator now, conduct a knowledge review with the departing partner while still available, and document the Project's scope and maintenance process.
options.D: Export all 18 knowledge documents to a shared drive as a backup, then reassign the Project.

items.question:
A procurement manager at a healthcare provider has a 75-page procurement playbook. Some queries require cross-section synthesis (e.g., how an approval threshold interacts with a vendor evaluation criterion). Other queries are section-specific (e.g., what is the threshold for a sole-source award). The manager must decide between splitting the document and keeping it whole with headings.

What is the BEST structural approach?

options.A: Split the playbook into separate files for each section to maximise retrieval precision for specific queries.
options.B: Keep the playbook as a flat document and rely on Claude to navigate it without structural aids.
options.C: Summarise each section into a shorter document to reduce the total volume.
options.D: Keep the document whole but add descriptive section headings to enable navigation for section-specific queries while preserving cross-section context.

items.question:
An investment analyst uses a Claude Project for portfolio analysis. She has a quarterly factor model with two distinct parts: a methodology section that changes annually when reviewed, and a parameter table that is updated each quarter with new factor loadings. She is deciding how to structure this in the Project.

What is the MOST appropriate approach?

options.A: Keep the methodology section in Project knowledge as a stable reference and upload the parameter table per-chat each quarter when it is refreshed.
options.B: Add the full document to Project knowledge and re-upload the full document each quarter when the parameters are updated.
options.C: Add only the parameter table to Project knowledge and rely on per-chat prompts for methodology context.
options.D: Configure a connector for the full document since part of it changes quarterly.

items.question:
A managing partner at a 50-person consulting firm has created a single Claude Project shared with all 50 consultants. Project knowledge contains each client's strategy deck, financial model, and engagement letter — 15 clients total. The partner believes this maximises context for the whole team.

What is the MOST significant architectural problem?

options.A: The knowledge base volume is too large for a single Project to serve reliably.
options.B: Every consultant can access every client's confidential strategy and financial information through the shared Project, violating client confidentiality obligations.
options.C: The Project should be limited to one client at a time to prevent response quality degradation.
options.D: Strategy decks contain forward-looking projections that may conflict with publicly available information.

items.question:
A data architect at an insurance company is designing the knowledge architecture for a Claude Project used by underwriters. The Project will use three knowledge sources: a product rate manual (updated annually); underwriting guidelines (revised monthly as risk appetite changes); live premium rates refreshed hourly from the pricing system.

What is the MOST appropriate architecture?

options.A: Use connectors for all three to ensure uniform synchronisation across the knowledge base.
options.B: Use static uploads for all three and refresh each on its own schedule.
options.C: Static upload with annual review for the rate manual, static upload with monthly replacement for the underwriting guidelines, and a connector for the live premium rates.
options.D: Use a connector for any knowledge source that changes more frequently than quarterly.
